Per row: {closed_on, target_name, kind, status, scale_metrics, integration_target, affected_subcap_ids[], maturity_effect, effect_note, e_ids[]}. closed_on REQUIRED to the month; announced-but-not-closed is a SEPARATE row with status=ANNOUNCED and its own date. status ANNOUNCED|INTEGRATING|COMPLETE|ABANDONED — never NULL. scale_metrics quantified in the acquirer's own terms: branches, deposits or loan volume, members/customers, FTE. integration_target the date integration is tracking to, where stated (date|null). maturity_effect ADVANCED|CONSTRAINED|NEUTRAL|TEMPORARILY_CONSTRAINED with the named cells — TEMPORARILY_CONSTRAINED is honest and often correct during a cutover; do not smooth it to NEUTRAL. effect_note 20-45 words: what the integration does to the named capability and over what window — specific cell, direction, window. CROSS-SURFACE (emit once, hand to three): every acquisition is also a TIMELINE event with kind=M&A; an integration in flight is a COST OF ACTING NOW input for the why-now and a timing constraint for the roadmap; all three must carry the same date and the same direction of effect. Gates: every row dated and cited; status never NULL; affected cells resolve; consistent with C1 and O3.

_notes: Layer/status vocabulary is settled by the Surface Spec's own 'Vocabulary resolved' paragraph and the CLAUDE.md corrections table (binding): layer keys are OPS|CUST|DATA|INFRA — never L2-L5 (they collide with the L1-L4 evidence levels rendered on the same card) — and every register row carries status CONFIRMED|INFERRED|CLAIMED|ABSENT, required per row, without which the T2 landscape strip cannot be recomputed. The Surface Spec's original T1 prompt block ({vendor, product, layer, confidence, as_of, e_ids[]} with layer enum core|crm|data|integration|channel|security) is superseded; the skill's REISSUED prompt shape is the operative one. 'confidence' from the original prompt does not survive the resolution — confidence never stands in for evidence; status replaces it.

TRD representative contract names the item field 'name' where the Surface Spec prompt and the skill use 'product' ('vendor and product are separate fields'); product wins per the Surface Spec's payload-shapes-are-law authority for this extraction.

The TRD representative contract nests the T2 landscape tiles under this section as 'landscape'; the section registry (TRD + Backend Schema) serves T2 from insights.landscape (serving table insights_landscape). The registry rules on placement; either way the landscape counts must be recomputed from and reconcile to this register (counts computed, never stored).

compliance_attestations appears in the Surface Spec's Information sources table ('where the client states one') and the TRD representative contract, but not in the skill's REISSUED prompt or section_templates.json; carried here as optional with item shape unstated.

T3 (platform detail sub-page) reads this same section — detection basis, evidence, the cells it touches and the gap it leaves; detection_basis and linked_subcap_ids are what it renders. No separate section exists.

items.doc: The client's actual stack, each entry a PRODUCT with its vendor and evidence. Per item: {ts_id, vendor, product, layer, pillar_id, status, evidence_level, detection_basis, as_of, linked_subcap_ids[], e_ids[]}. A PRODUCT, not a service and not a category — 'Salesforce Financial Services Cloud' is a product; 'CRM', 'Analytics/BI', 'Django' are not; vendor and product are separate fields. layer OPS|CUST|DATA|INFRA (OPS=Operations & core banking, P3 · CUST=Customer engagement, P2, primary gap · DATA=Data & analytics, P4 · INFRA=Infrastructure & cloud, P4) — NOT L2-L5, those keys collide with the L1-L4 evidence levels on the same card. status CONFIRMED|INFERRED|CLAIMED|ABSENT, REQUIRED on every row — the landscape strip recomputes its four counts from this field; without it the strip is uncomputable. evidence_level L1-L4, and it governs the verb the prose may use — CONFIRMED is Evidence Level 1-2 and requires a T1/T2 source; a CONFIRMED row without a citation is a defect, not a style (either the citation was dropped or the status should be INFERRED; confidence never stands in for evidence); an ABSENT row backed by a demand signal (e.g. job postings) licenses 'signals suggest', never 'uses'. detection_basis one clause, printed on the detail page (T3). Every item cites the evidence that places it in this client's estate — an item you cannot cite is a rumour: put it in dropped[] with the reason. ts_id agent-minted (TS-nnn). dma_impact, peer_coverage and peer_deployments are OPTIONAL per row and are the drilldown's explanation. dma_impact: 40-90 words saying WHICH of this row's linked_subcap_ids the product bears on, what it reaches and what it does not, and by what mechanism — the cells and their scores are already served, so this field is the reasoning that connects them. Never derive or restate a score, never project an uplift (no source states one), and frame what is not covered as available value rather than as a failing: 'the estate does not yet reach X', never 'the vendor fails to X'. peer_coverage: a share in 0..1 of the run's NAMED peer set publicly running this product — a percentage sent as 62 rather than 0.62 is refused. peer_deployments: the per-peer breakdown behind that share, [{peer, deployed, basis, source_url, as_of}], one row per peer INCLUDING the peers you could not establish (deployed: null) — a coverage figure of 2/5 with three unknowns is not 2/5, and the card has to be able to say so. A technographic claim about a named institution is a research finding: without source_url and as_of it is not one.

layers.doc: Layer rollup, per layer: {layer, pillar_id, detected, expected, is_primary_gap}. Four layer cards — operations, customer engagement, data, infrastructure — each with a pillar tag and a detection count ('2 of 4 detected'). The layering is the analysis: detected-of-expected at a layer with a pillar tag says where the gap is and which pillar absorbs it. is_primary_gap is a semantic flag — PRIMARY GAP LAYER is a judgement the surface makes explicitly; no colour in the payload.

dropped.doc: Per dropped candidate: {candidate, reason} — candidates rejected by the taxonomy, with the reason. dropped[] is reported, not hidden: it is how a taxonomy gap becomes visible. MAY BE EMPTY: a run that dropped no candidate has an empty list, and that is the ordinary case rather than a finding — so CG-17 does not require an empty_state for it. Every other required list on this page does.

compliance_attestations.doc: Client-stated compliance attestations (e.g. 'SOC 2 Type II'), one string per attestation, from profile/research only — never inferred from a vendor's marketing. The Surface Spec names the field without an item shape; kept as plain strings, cited via the envelope e_ids.
